summary: The IPv4 header carries the fields routers need to forward a datagram: addresses, length, fragmentation controls, time to live, the upper-layer protocol, and a header checksum. It is 20 bytes plus up to 40 bytes of options.

sections.heading: Fields
bullets: IHL (4 bits): header length in 32-bit words; minimum 5 (20 bytes), maximum 15 (60 bytes).
Type of Service / DSCP+ECN (8 bits): QoS marking and congestion notification.
Total Length (16 bits): header plus data in bytes; maximum 65,535.
Identification (16): shared by all fragments of one datagram.
Flags (3): reserved, DF (Don't Fragment), MF (More Fragments).
Fragment Offset (13): position of this fragment in 8-byte units.
TTL (8): decremented at each router; at zero the packet is dropped and ICMP Time Exceeded is sent.
Protocol (8): payload type, e.g. 1 ICMP, 6 TCP, 17 UDP.
Header Checksum (16): covers the header only.

sections.heading: Header checksum
sections.body: The checksum is the 16-bit one's complement of the one's complement sum of all 16-bit header words, computed with the checksum field set to zero. Because TTL changes at every hop, each router recomputes it (usually incrementally).
sections.code:
sum = 0
for each 16-bit word w in header: sum += w
while (sum >> 16): sum = (sum & 0xffff) + (sum >> 16)
checksum = ~sum & 0xffff

sections.heading: Fragmentation
sections.body: If a datagram exceeds the next link's MTU and DF is clear, a router splits it. Each fragment repeats the header, sets MF on all but the last, and stores its byte offset divided by 8 in the offset field. The destination, not routers, reassembles using source, destination, protocol, and Identification.
sections.code:
MTU 1500, payload 4000 bytes (header 20):
  frag 1: offset 0,   1480 bytes, MF=1
  frag 2: offset 185, 1480 bytes, MF=1   (1480/8 = 185)
  frag 3: offset 370, 1040 bytes, MF=0

sections.body: Senders set DF and shrink packets when a router answers ICMP 'Fragmentation needed' (type 3, code 4). Blocking that ICMP message creates black holes where large packets vanish but small ones work.
RFC 791 defined classes A (/8), B (/16), and C (/24) by leading bits. Classless addressing (CIDR, RFC 4632) replaced them so any prefix length can be used and routes can be aggregated.
Record Route, Timestamp, and Source Route options exist but are often dropped by routers for security and performance, which is one reason IPv6 removed them from the base header.

takeaways: 20-byte base header; IHL tells you where options end.
TTL prevents loops; Protocol selects TCP, UDP, or ICMP.
Fragmentation uses ID, MF, DF, and an offset in 8-byte units.
The checksum covers the header only and is recomputed per hop.
